g.text: HC-SR04 ranging - the protocol engine on both sides
STATUS: RED - 5 checks fail; the CONVERSION is proven on measurement 0, the second measurement is not reached
FIRMWARE SIDE - firmware/sr04_range.pe
PINS
TRIG = pin 6 (SR_TRIG, 0x40), DRIVEN by us
ECHO = pin 5 (SR_ECHO, 0x20), RELEASED
and READ BACK as the pad
TWO SEPARATE PADS, because the host drives one
and listens on the other. Writing a level and
an enable together - the idiom the other acts
use - is impossible here, and the firmware does
not try: dmem[5] is the level and PINOE is the
enable, and they are written on purpose.
TRIGGER
a 10 us pulse
TXPIN = SR_TRIG, PINOE = SR_TRIG, then a
COUNTED delay, then release.
EXACT IN CLOCKS: 4 * SR_TRIG + 4, and SR_TRIG = 149
makes that 600 clocks = 10.000 us exactly.
MEASURED 601 CLOCKS = 10.0167 us.
The device
asks for 10 us MINIMUM so the extra clock is
harmless to a real sensor - and the check is an
equality anyway, because the act claims the
count and not a datasheet floor.
The constant is a COUNT OF INSTRUCTIONS and not
microseconds, which is why it lives in peasm's
CONSTS and why the act can be perturbed through
--const at all.
RECOVERY
wait for the sensor
SR_RECOV_LEN = 117 on (4,40):
the stated 120 615 clocks = 2 010 us, which
clears the sensor's own settling time
AND ITS ABSENCE WAS A REAL DEFECT:
the device
needs a moment after the trigger before ECHO
means anything, and a program that measures the
line immediately is reading the recovery.
MEASURED: the model saw only ONE trigger,
so this
path is where the second measurement is lost.
see the open-defect note for the status.
STATE MACHINE in dmem[13], 0..4, dispatched by a
cumulative subtract chain.
WAIT FOR THE ECHO'S RISING EDGE
spin on the pad until ECHO goes high.
THE ECHO IS CAPTURED, NOT SAMPLED,
which is
what makes this act safe at 4 m: the answer is
the WIDTH of a pulse, and a width does not care
when you looked at it.
MEASURE
t = the echo width in us
the 1 us counter read as a DIFFERENCE,
exactly as in freqmeter.pe and for the same
reason: the clear-on-read flag on port 6 is ONE
BIT, so a poll loop longer than a tick reports
several ticks as one.
THERE IS NO 16-BIT SUBTRACT HERE EITHER,
and for
the same reason as the meter: the counter is RESET
at the echo's rising edge and read at its falling
edge, so the answer is whatever accumulated.
MEASURED 1160 us
against the model's 1160 us -
exact, and the check is 1 % with a 2 us floor.
CONVERT
mm = us * 11/64, exactly
THE CONVERSION IS THE ACT,
and it is where
the ISA bites. No multiply, no divide, no carry
flag - only JZ/JNZ.
us = 64q + r
EXACT, because 11q is an integer
So no 16x16 multiply, no division and no
approximation. The plan assumed a multiply; this
identity removes it.
Q = us >> 6 ACC = 11*(us & 63), then >> 6
T = 11*(us >> 6) T += ACC, and T is the answer
MEASURED 199 mm, expected 199 mm. EXACT.
BANK
the answer
dmem[10] is the measurement count, and
IT READS 01, NOT 02.
The firmware banked one
measurement; the second never ran. This is the
first of the five failing checks and it is a
symptom, not the fault - the cause is upstream, in
the trigger and recovery path.
STATUS: RED
5 checks fail, not in run_all.sh
measurement 0: echo 1160 us
-> firmware 1160 us -> 199 mm
-> EXPECTED 199 mm PASS
measurement 1: echo 5816 us
-> firmware 1160 us -> X mm
-> EXPECTED 999 mm FAIL
dmem[10] = 01: only ONE banked
the model saw 1 trigger, not 2
the trigger is 601 clocks, not 600
SENSOR MODEL - tb/tb_pe_soc_sr04.v
ARM
the model presents two targets, so the
firmware is asked for TWO measurements:
echo 1 160 us -> expect 199 mm
echo 5 816 us -> expect 999 mm
THE SECOND TARGET IS THE ONE THAT MAKES THE ACT
WORTH RUNNING: 1 160 us fits in twelve bits and
5 816 us does not, so the two together exercise the
ten-bit path and the high byte.
TRIGGER
detected
THE MODEL SAW EXACTLY 1 TRIGGER.
The check
carries its own explanation - "a trigger that is
driven rather than pulsed shows up here" - which is
the right way to write a failing check: the reader
learns the shape of the defect from the message.
CHECKS
FAIL the firmware banked both measurements
FAIL the model saw exactly 2 triggers
FAIL the trigger is EXACTLY 600 clocks (601)
FAIL measurement 1: 1160 us is outside 1 % of 5816
FAIL measurement 1: 1160 us is X mm, not 999 mm
AND NOTE WHAT IS NOT AMONG THEM:
no conversion
check failed, and no first-measurement check
failed. The arithmetic the act exists to demonstrate
is correct on the one measurement that ran.
A MULTIPLY BY ELEVEN IS FOUR DOUBLINGS AND TWO ADDS.
(5x is 4x + x, and 10x is 5x doubled.) No loop, no counter, no
second temporary: the multiplicand stays in Q throughout.
AND A DOUBLING IS THE CHEAPEST 16-BIT OPERATION THIS ISA
HAS, and unlike any other 16-bit add it needs NO both-zero
guard. The carry out of lo+lo is BIT 7 OF THE ORIGINAL
LOW BYTE, so one AND with 0x80 and one JNZ is the whole
test; and "the result is zero" means "nothing carried",
because doubling zero cannot carry and is the only way to
reach zero.
A general add of a variable IS different: 0 + 0 = 0 is not a
carry, so the addends must be re-read to tell a wrap from a
pair of zeros.
That asymmetry is the reason the conversion
is mostly doublings.
No 16-bit overflow is possible anywhere in the conversion,
and the
largest value involved is 11 * (23000 >> 6) = 3949: the intermediates
are 8q = 2872 and 10q = 3590, and the second term is
Recorded rather than assumed,
because an
unnoticed overflow in the high byte is invisible from the
outside - the answer would still be a plausible millimetre
figure.
THE 11/64 CONSTANT, AND WHY ITS ERROR IS STATED
RATHER THAN ABSORBED.
t (us) = 2 * d (mm) / 0.343 mm/us
+0.22 % long
against the speed of sound. That error belongs
to the CONSTANT, not to the arithmetic: the conversion below is EXACT for
11/64, which is a different and checkable claim from "the range is right to
two parts in a thousand", and only the first one can be asserted as an
equality.
WHAT IS KNOWN AND WHAT IS NOT, about the open defect.
The second measurement is lost, the bank holds one result, and the model saw one
trigger. The failure is therefore upstream of the conversion - in the path that
issues the second trigger and re-arms for the second echo - and NOT in the
arithmetic, which is exact on the measurement that did run.
WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED HERE:
which instruction is wrong. The five failing
checks say the second measurement does not happen; they do not say why, and a
figure that drew a cause would be drawing a hypothesis.
The 601-vs-600 trigger
is the most likely place to look - it is a one-instruction error of exactly
the kind this family has found six times - and it is stated as a place to look,
not as the fault.
